An undocumented PhaaS kit family using AI-assisted development is running device code phishing at scale: more than 70 active panels identified under names including BlackApex, DarkApex, SPY, and XXX101, all sharing a single backend engine.  Key findings:  - The kit abuses Microsoft's OAuth 2.0 device code flow. The attacker's backend requests a code, presents it to the victim inside a themed lure (SharePoint, Zoom, OneDrive, Adobe Acrobat Sign, Microsoft Excel), and the victim pastes it into the real login.microsoftonline[.]com/common/oauth2/deviceauth page. MFA is satisfied by the victim on Microsoft's own infrastructure, so the attacker's server redeems the code and receives a live access token, refresh token, and critically a Primary Refresh Token. That PRT is displayed in the admin panel and used to access mailboxes. The report compares PRT compromise to a Golden Ticket attack in on-premises AD because it enables SSO across integrated Entra ID applications.  - Delivery chains route through trusted services to evade reputation filtering. One chain uses a Google Share Link landing on a fake document-opening prompt. The second uses a PDF attachment linking through a legitimate Microsoft Forms page (forms[.]cloud[.]microsoft) before redirecting to the device code lure. Both terminate at Microsoft's real deviceauth page, and the sign-in shows "Microsoft Authentication Broker" on a device in the United States 🇺🇸, which is the attacker's backend, not the victim's.  - The LevelBlue SpiderLabs report makes a high-confidence assessment that the kit was built largely through AI-assisted development. Indicators: every function carries a "// Helper:" comment, verbose emoji-annotated console logs appear across lures and config files, defensive polish (isPolling flag, 14-minute code refresh timed against Microsoft's 15-minute expiry, separate mobile and desktop popup logic) is inconsistent with throwaway phishing infrastructure, and all five lures share identical backend contracts and retry logic despite completely different surfaces. The code is unobfuscated throughout.  - Operators exposed their own infrastructure. The kit's robots.txt lists /admin and /api paths. Pivoting on the SHA-256 body hash of that file in Censys (query in the report) returned more than 70 URLs hosting the same admin panel, mostly on ports 5000 and 443 across bulletproof hosting ASNs. Multiple API endpoints inside the panels were reportedly accessible without authentication, exposing dashboard statistics, domain management, session logs, anti-bot controls, and messaging integrations.  - The IOC table in the report lists VPS IPs and landing-page domains for all identified panel instances. Representative defanged samples: 95.133.228[.]253:5000 / 1mdrvpdf-rfqonlineinvite[.]com ([@]globaltoken1), 146.190.66[.]199:443 / arcomplianceservices[.]cfd (BlackApex), 199.192.20[.]82:443 / hsuonoormidimostrareguillarianmelengueleandoinfundieseis[.]fit (SPY), 37.10.71[.]147:443 / aaqkadnmmwuxntg2l.apiaccoumtsvcdocushare[.]icu (XXX101-TOKEN). Full table is in the report.  Hunt in Microsoft Entra ID sign-in logs for deviceCodeFlow authentication events, especially those originating from unmanaged devices, unfamiliar user agents, or IPs not associated with your environment. A sign-in showing "Microsoft Authentication Broker" as the client application initiated from an unexpected geography is a concrete detection signal this kit leaves behind. Where device code flow is not a business requirement, block it via Conditional Access. Where it is required, scope it to compliant devices and named locations only. IOCs are in the LevelBlue SpiderLabs report.  #DFIR_Radar

October 2026 roundup: CVE-2026-65660 reclassified from spoofing to RCE after active exploitation, EvilTokens phishing service dismantled, and unauthenticated Atlassian file read drew honeypot hits within two hours of a public PoC.  Key findings:  - CVE-2026-65660 shipped August 11 as a CVSS 6.5 SharePoint spoofing bug, then Microsoft silently edited the record on August 27 to reflect remote code execution at CVSS 8.8. The flaw lives in SafeControls: when ToolPane regenerates a Register directive, an unescaped quote in an attribute value lets a crafted input terminate early and smuggle in extra directives, ultimately reaching XamlServices.Parse() for deserialization and in-memory webshell execution. Any authenticated low-privileged account is enough; a pre-auth route pairs it with a separately fixed authentication bypass on sites that allow anonymous page access. Exploitation began September 24 per Previdian, CISA added it to KEV on September 25 with a September 28 federal remediation deadline under Binding Operational Directive 26-04, which also requires agencies to determine whether compromise preceded the patch. Affected products: SharePoint Enterprise Server 2016, SharePoint Server 2019, and SharePoint Server Subscription Edition.  - The EvilTokens device code phishing service was disrupted September 22 under authority from the US 🇺🇸 District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia, with 50 websites seized and more than 150 supporting domains disabled. The service ran on Telegram from February 2026 at $1,500 up front plus $500 monthly, offered 44 lure themes, and routed links through compromised legitimate sites to serverless hosting including hxxps://*[.]vercel[.]app and hxxps://*[.]workers[.]dev. Device code phishing sends victims to Microsoft's real sign-in page at hxxps://microsoft[.]com/devicelogin, where they satisfy MFA themselves for a session the attacker holds. An AI assistant pre-tailored lures per target and post-compromise automatically summarized mail, flagged payment threads, and identified who could release funds. Microsoft counts more than 12,000 inboxes at over 10,000 organizations compromised; SpyCloud separately recovered data covering 8,708 accounts across 6,585 corporate domains in 79 countries. Coinbase traced roughly $1.1 million through four Tron addresses. Two suspected operators were detained in London on September 11.  - CVE-2026-21589, rated CVSS v4.0 9.3, is an unauthenticated file read across eight self-hosted Atlassian Data Center products (Jira Software, Jira Service Management, Confluence, Bitbucket, Bamboo, Crowd, Crucible, Fisheye). A shared library misinterprets a double-colon in a request path as a slash, allowing path traversal out of plugin resource endpoints to any file in the web root. No authentication is required. Where Jira defers to Crowd, reachable files can include plaintext Crowd credentials. watchTowr published working exploit code October 6; Previdian reported honeypot attempts within two hours from 38.60.157[.]86, 146.70.187[.]234, and 159.26.119[.]225, and noted a Nuclei template had since appeared. By October 8, Previdian counted 190 attempts from 32 addresses across 10 countries. CISA added it to KEV on October 15.  - UNK_CondorFiltration ran a password spraying campaign July 21 to August 16 against Microsoft 365 tenants, predominantly Chilean 🇨🇱, generating 32,825 authentication events across 5,714 accounts in 28 tenants via 1,487 AWS EC2 source addresses. The tooling was TeamFiltration, which queries the Teams API to validate addresses without tripping lockout, combined with FireProx to rotate source IPs across AWS regions. Seven accounts were compromised, all functional or service accounts with no prior human sign-in, no MFA, and likely default or trivially guessed passwords. Six fell within seven minutes. Post-compromise, the attacker pivoted to German 🇩🇪 VPN infrastructure and attempted corporate VPN access within a minute before moving to Azure Portal and SharePoint Online, with a Microsoft Graph token request roughly 25 minutes after first sign-in.  Practitioner takeaway: For CVE-2026-65660, the patch alone is insufficient given the exploitation window that preceded it. Hunt on-premises SharePoint for unexpected registered .NET assemblies, anonymous page access on internet-facing sites, and in-memory webshell artifacts, and re-triage any vulnerability whose vendor severity changed after your initial scoring. For CVE-2026-21589, IOCs from Previdian's honeypots are in the report. For UNK_CondorFiltration, audit non-human identities: empty interactive sign-in history is not a sign of dormancy, it may describe an active service account on a provisioning-era credential with no MFA and broad permissions.  #DFIR_Radar

Poisoned Claude Code VS Code extension planted an SSH backdoor on up to 5,000 developer machines via Open VSX, surviving editor close, reboot, and extension removal with cross-platform persistence.  Key findings:  - The malicious payload was version 2.1.313 of the Claude Code extension, published to the Open VSX marketplace (not Microsoft's Visual Studio Marketplace) and live for roughly 11 hours on October 29, 2026. Editors that depend on Open VSX because they cannot use the Microsoft store, specifically Cursor and Windsurf, were the exposure surface. The Eclipse Foundation-run marketplace carried the compromised build; Anthropic did not publish it.  - The injected code is an IIFE prepended to the legitimate minified bundle, so it executes via Node.js before the extension's normal activate callback runs. No user interaction is required. It uses standard Node modules (child_process, fs, os, path, http, crypto) and immediately writes an attacker SSH key to the victim's authorized_keys file, then opens an outbound SSH tunnel back to the attacker's server. The tunnel persists after the editor closes and retries the connection roughly every 60 seconds.  - Persistence is cross-platform. On macOS it drops a launchd-style startup file using an Apple-style name. On Linux it adds a cron entry that runs at reboot. On Windows it attempts to create a scheduled task named SysMon, falling back to the Startup folder. This survives a reboot regardless of whether the extension is still installed.  - The payload beacons the machine's hostname, username, OS, home directory, working directory, Git email, and public IP to the operator. It also reports the names of up to 40 environment variables that pattern-match against keys, tokens, passwords, and AWS/GCP credentials, giving the attacker a triage inventory of which machines hold cloud access worth targeting next.  - A faulty privilege check on macOS often prevents the payload from enabling Remote Login, reducing SSH backdoor utility on Macs where the service was already off. However persistence and reconnaissance still fire. On hosts where SSH was already enabled, or is enabled later, the planted svc-telemetry key is ready to use. Cursor worked with the attacker's cloud provider to take the C2 server offline, breaking the tunnel and the data exfil channel.  Takeaway: Uninstalling the extension does not remove the backdoor. For any machine that had version 2.1.313 installed, the response steps are: inspect the SSH authorized_keys file for an entry labelled svc-telemetry and remove it; audit launchd plists (macOS), crontab entries (Linux), and scheduled tasks plus the Startup folder (Windows) for persistence artefacts tied to this payload; then check SSH logs for logins from localhost authenticating with the svc-telemetry key to determine whether an operator gained interactive access. Isolate the host, rotate every credential and session the machine could reach (cloud tokens, API keys, Git credentials) from a clean system, and consider a rebuild. Cursor and Phorion have both published cleanup scripts and indicators of compromise.  #DFIR_Radar

sample_tweets.text: 🚨 The Binance security incident is a massive wake-up call for the entire crypto industry.  With an estimated $6.3B in exposure, this case goes far beyond a typical wallet exploit. Initial findings point to a compromised DevOps environment, raising serious questions about operational security and infrastructure vulnerabilities.  What's particularly striking is the scale of the response: nearly $3B in assets reportedly frozen through collaboration between Binance and blockchain partners. Meanwhile, Binance has committed to covering all losses through its corporate funds and SAFU.  But let's be clear: this isn't just about Binance. It's about the security standards of the entire crypto ecosystem.  🔍 My take: Self-custody, infrastructure security, real-time monitoring, and cross-industry cooperation are becoming more important than ever. Trust in crypto must be backed by solid security, not just promises.  💬 Do you think this incident will push exchanges to completely rethink their security architecture, or are we still underestimating the risks?  👇 Drop your thoughts below!  Crypto has challenges, but every major security lesson is an opportunity to build a stronger, more resilient industry 🚀

🇮🇷| Friday in Tehran: A Qatari Envoy, a Blazing Strait of Hormuz, and a Warning from the Pulpit  October 30, 2026. Tehran. Three pieces of news arrived on the same day. They are not three separate events; rather, they are three dimensions of a single, unified strategy.  💥 The First Front: A Qatari Envoy  A high-level Qatari delegation has arrived in Tehran, led by a senior advisor to the Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of Qatar. They are holding a series of talks with top Iranian officials.  This delegation has not come to "mediate," it has come to "deliver a message."  A few days ago, *The New York Times* reported that U.S. Vice President Vance sent a letter to Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council. The letter was relayed via Qatar. Its contents included a proposal for meetings between U.S. and Iranian officials, the immediate resumption of comprehensive negotiations, and a commitment that Vance himself would lead the American team.  Qatar serves as the conduit. It acts simultaneously as the host for the Al Udeid Air Base and as an interlocutor for Iran. It is not merely a "neutral post office"; it is a channel and the function of a channel is to transmit information, not to alter it.  Vance’s letter is, in essence, a "request for an honorable exit." Eight months of war. $43.6 billion spent. 21 U.S. service members dead, 865 wounded. Bases in eight different countries struck by Iranian missiles. An E-3 AWACS aircraft destroyed. An F-35 fighter jet transmitting a 7700 emergency squawk code. Aircraft carriers forced to withdraw from the Red Sea. Elections looming. Oil prices rising.  The Qatari delegation is in Tehran today to ask: What is Rezaei’s response?  🎯 The Second Front: A Warning from the Pulpit  Mohammad Javad Haj-Ali-Akbari, the prayer leader for Friday congregational prayers in Tehran, delivered a statement from the pulpit, a statement intended to set the tone for the entire nation.  “The Iranian people have extensive experience with the conduct of the United States; they know that requests for negotiations, the delivery of letters, and the dispatch of intermediaries do not necessarily signify a reduction in the threat. Therefore, one should not be deceived by such maneuvers.”  “Past experience shows that at certain junctures when the other side speaks of negotiations, sends letters, or dispatches intermediaries more severe risks may well be looming on the horizon.”  “The Iranian people are well-acquainted with the track record of U.S. actions; they will not be misled by a diplomatic facade, but rather assess the situation based on historical experience and the actual conduct of the other party.”  This is not mere “anti-American rhetoric.” It is “wartime discipline.” Akbari is telling the entire nation: the Qatari delegation is in Tehran, and a letter from Vance lies on the table, yet the threat has not diminished. Do not let the word “diplomacy” lull you into a false sense of security; “diplomacy” can serve as a cover for a preparatory phase.  He points to history: the coup of August 1953, in which the U.S. and the U.K. toppled the democratically elected government of Mossadegh; the assassination of Soleimani; the “Twelve-Day War”; the “Forty-Day War.” He argues that the U.S. shifted from indirect intervention to direct confrontation not out of strength, but because all other avenues had failed. When their plans did not work, the U.S. turned to direct confrontation. Yet, the Iranian people remain standing in resistance.  “Do not be deceived by these maneuvers.” This message is directed not only at the worshippers in Tehran, but at Iranian society as a whole, a nation currently squeezed between signals of negotiation and the specter of military threat.  📜 The Third Front: The Burning of the Strait of Hormuz  The Navy of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) announced that two oil tankers were intercepted in the southern waters of the Strait of Hormuz—one in the eastern sector and one in the western sector. Both had deactivated their navigation and positioning systems, attempting to traverse unauthorized routes “with the support of the American terrorist military.” Radio warnings were ignored. They entered a dangerous zone. An incident occurred. They were brought to a halt.  The regular Navy of the Iranian Armed Forces announced the destruction of an enemy unmanned surface vessel (USV). Two non-compliant oil tankers struck mines in the eastern Strait of Hormuz, sustaining damage and catching fire.  “Full responsibility lies with the tanker owners.”  The Revolutionary Guard has announced that a third supertanker carrying over 2 million barrels of crude oil struck a mine near the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz. It caught fire, was abandoned, and remains ablaze.  Three supertankers in a single day. Including previous incidents, six vessels have been struck or hit mines this week alone.  This is not an “escalation.” It is “enforcement.” Vessels that disable their tracking systems, enter prohibited zones, ignore warnings, and attempt to smuggle oil under the “protection” of the U.S. Navy will strike mines. They will burn. They will be abandoned. Iran writes the rules and enforces them with missiles, naval mines, and unmanned surface vessels.  A statement from the IRGC Navy makes it clear: “Any movement, infiltration, or provocation within the surveillance range of the Armed Forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran will be met with a firm and proportionate response.”  ⚔️ Three tracks, one logic:  The Qatari envoy: Diplomatic channels. A letter from Vance. A request for a dignified exit. Delivering a message. Warnings from the pulpit: Wartime discipline. Do not be lulled into complacency by talk of “negotiations.” The threat has not diminished; history speaks for itself. Flames in the Strait of Hormuz: Military enforcement. Three tankers. Six vessels. The rules are being strictly enforced.  These three tracks are not contradictory; they are components of a single wartime apparatus.  Diplomacy conveys messages; ideology maintains vigilance; the military enforces the rules. The simultaneous pursuit of diplomatic negotiation and military enforcement is not a “contradiction,” it is “coordination.”  Vance’s letter was sent under the weight of military pressure, a pressure that did not cease after the letter was delivered. Tankers are burning; unmanned vessels are being destroyed; the rules of the Strait of Hormuz are being enforced. This is not a case of “negotiating while fighting”; it is a case of “defining the terms of negotiation through combat.”  What Akbari stated from the pulpit is this: Do not be pacified by the word “negotiation,” for such talks may merely be preparation for the next round of attacks. The burning tankers in the Strait of Hormuz serve as a physical footnote to that very warning.    🔻 The Mirror  Washington says: We send letters; we seek diplomacy.  Tehran says: Your letters lie on the table. Your oil tankers are burning. Your bases have been struck. Your aircraft carriers have retreated. Your F-35s have signaled an emergency (squawk 7700). Your elections are approaching. You are looking for a way out, a face-saving exit. Yet, we have not stopped.  Qatar says: We shall act as messengers.  Iran says: You are welcome. But the terms remain unchanged. Seven conditions. The U.S. must fulfill its obligations first. Enriched uranium will remain within our borders. The rules for the Strait of Hormuz shall be written by us.  Akbari says: Do not be deceived.  The Strait of Hormuz says: Three oil tankers are burning.  A nation that, in the eighth month of a war, remains capable of simultaneously managing diplomacy, ideology, and military enforcement is not merely "responding to a crisis." It is *managing* the crisis controlling its tempo, defining its boundaries, and dictating the distribution of its costs.  Today in Tehran, the Qatari delegation did not hear, "We will consider it." They heard, "The terms remain unchanged." And the fires in the Strait of Hormuz serve as the physical evidence that those terms remain unchanged.  Long live Iran. Long live the Resistance. Long live the Axis of Resistance.

@binance  commitment to fully cover the roughly $6.3 billion impact from the hot-wallet incident is backed by concrete actions already underway.   The exchange has reserved more than $6.34 billion in company funds, with about $5 billion already held in the exact tokens affected, and is actively purchasing the rest through market and OTC channels to eliminate shortfalls. Roughly $3 billion has been frozen on-chain through coordination with law enforcement, issuers, and blockchain partner, figures that exclude those frozen amounts and will be publicly verified through an updated Proof of Reserves once remediation is complete.   Independent reporting from outlets tracking the on-chain data aligns with Binance’s stated impact and response, reinforcing that user balances are being protected by both the SAFU fund and corporate resources  The preliminary investigation points to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop that enabled unauthorized withdrawal transactions through a service container, with no evidence of private-key leakage. Binance has identified additional breach points, revoked affected authorizations, and is working around the clock with industry partners to recover more assets while completing a security revamp of its withdrawal systems.   This layered response; freezing funds, matching token holdings, and committing company capital shows the exchange treating the event as a platform-level liability rather than shifting losses to users, consistent with its long-standing SAFU framework established for extreme scenarios.  Users should rely exclusively on official Binance channels for updates and ignore any unsolicited messages claiming to help with recovery or withdrawals, as phishing attempts often spike after high-profile incidents.   Enable or review two-factor authentication, withdrawal address whitelists, and device security on your accounts, and monitor the forthcoming Proof of Reserves snapshot for confirmation that holdings match customer balances.   Withdrawals are paused while the security overhaul finishes and are expected to resume in the coming days; patience here reduces risk, and long-term diversification of holdings across platforms and self-custody options remains sound practice regardless of any single event.

【Linuxカーネルに深刻度9.8（最大級）の脆弱性。WSL2とDockerの人はapt upgradeじゃ直りません】  脆弱性の対応、日々お疲れ様です Chromeに続いて、さらに来ました。今度はLinuxです ただ今回は「全員今すぐ」の話ではないので、先に落ち着いて読んでください 少し長いですが詳しくまとめたので、自分の環境の見出しだけでも読んでもらえると嬉しいです  何の話か CVE-2026-98432というLinuxカーネルのバグです（10月15日公開） 先日書いたChromeの大量修正にも関わっている、Anthropicの10月27日の発表（Claudeの未公開モデルが見つけた穴） その中のLinuxの1本です 2015年から入っていたバグなので、現役のLinuxはほぼ全部該当します CVEの記録上のスコアは10点満点の9.8です  中身 外から細工した接続要求を送りつけられるだけで、ログインも要らずに起きます 接続要求の処理が別のCPUで同時に走った時に、消したはずのメモリを読みに行くバグで、起きた時に一番ありそうなのはサーバーごと落ちる（クラッシュ）です IPv4の話で、IPv6は今回のバグの対象外です  条件が揃えば外からrootでコマンドを実行できるところまでAnthropicは実証したと発表しています ただ報道によるとその条件は「Multipath TCPで待ち受けているサーバー」で、これは複数回線を束ねる拡張で、アプリ側で明示的に使う設定が要るものです 普通の設定のWebサーバーがそのまま当てはまるかは、まだ分かりません 対象は、外に向けて待ち受けているサービスがある機械です Webだけでなく、SSHの22番を開けているだけで該当するので、開発用のVPSもほぼ全部です 逆に、外に向けて何も待ち受けていない機械には刺さる場所がありません AndroidやNAS、ルーター、ラズパイも中身はLinuxですが、考え方は同じで、外に待ち受けを開けていなければ急ぎではなく、修正はメーカー待ちです  温度感は配布元で割れています UbuntuはHigh Red Hatは現実的な被害は落ちるまでという見方でModerate、修正は今後の更新に回しています  悪用された報告は今のところ見当たりません なので「全員今すぐ」ではなく、自分がどのケースか見て、出た修正を当てる、で十分かなと思います  クラウドやVPSで公開サーバーを動かしている人 配布元の修正が出たら当てて、再起動（カーネルは再起動して初めて効きます） Debianはもう出ています（12は6.1.190、13は6.12.113） Ubuntuは10月30日時点でも22.04、24.04とも作業中で、今apt upgradeしても当たるものはまだありません 出た時の番号は24.04が6.8.0-149、22.04が5.15.0-203の予定なので、uname -rがそれ以上になれば修正済みです 20.04以前は通常サポートが終わっているので、修正が来るとしてもUbuntu Pro（個人なら5台まで無料）に入っている人だけです  Amazon Linux 2023は6.12系と6.18系のカーネルは修正済み、標準の6.1系とAmazon Linux 2はまだです  Red Hat系（RHEL、AlmaLinux、Rocky）は配布元の判断で修正が後になるので、下のつなぎで待つ形です  修正が来るまでのつなぎ 公式の回避策は、UbuntuもRed HatもSUSEも出していません その上で、仕組みから言えることが2つあります  1つ目は露出を減らすこと SSHや管理画面は接続元を自分のIPに絞る CloudflareやALBのような前段を挟む場合は、本体側で前段のIP以外を遮断して初めて意味があります（NLBのようにL4で素通しするタイプは別）  2つ目はIPオプションを落とすこと バグが触るのは接続要求に付いていたIPオプションのメモリなので、IPオプション付きのTCPパケットを手前で落とせば、理屈上はこの経路に入りません（nftablesならip hdrlength > 5を条件にdrop） TCPだけに絞るのは、他のプロトコルには正規で付くことがあるからです ufwのような簡易ツールでは書けないので、nftablesかiptablesを直接触れる人向けで、自分の環境で試してからにしてください 有償のライブパッチ（KernelCareなど）はDebian 13向けが先に出ています Ubuntu ProのLivepatchは確認できていません  WSL2の人 カーネルはUbuntuの中ではなく、Microsoftが配っています ここがややこしいのですが、Ubuntuの中でapt upgradeしても、カーネルは1ミリも変わりません 更新はPowerShellでwsl --update（かWindows Update） そのあとwsl --shutdownで一度止めると、次の起動から新しいカーネルになります  Microsoftは修正入りのカーネル（6.18.58.1）をここ数日で公開していますが、wsl --updateで降ってくる版に入ったかはまだ確認できていません WSLの中でuname -rを打って、6.18.56以上なら修正済み、今配られている6.18.33系や、古いままの6.6系・5.15系なら未修正です （WSL1はLinuxカーネルを使っていないので関係ありません）  Dockerの人 コンテナはホストのカーネルをそのまま使うので、コンテナの中で更新しても意味がありません LinuxのサーバーならホストのOSを更新 WindowsのDocker Desktopは標準のWSL2バックエンドならWSL2のカーネルで動いているので、上と同じwsl --update MacのDocker Desktopは自前のカーネルなので、Docker Desktop本体の更新です（修正入りの版が出たかは未確認） OrbStackやColima、Rancher Desktopも同じで、VMのカーネルを配っているのが誰かで決まります  Hyper-VやVirtualBox、VMwareの仮想マシンの人 これだけはゲストの中でapt upgradeで合っています（配布元の修正が出てから）  自分のカーネルの番号はuname -rで出ます 修正済みは5.10.272、5.15.223、6.1.190、6.6.159、6.12.113、6.18.56、7.2.10以上です ただしこれは、WSL2やArch、Amazon Linuxのように上流の番号をそのまま使っている環境向けの目安です Ubuntu、Debian、Red Hat系は番号の付け方が違って上の番号とは比べられないので、配布元の案内（Ubuntuは上に書いた予定の番号）で見てください  自宅のWSL2や仮想マシンは、外から直接つながる構成（ブリッジ接続やポート開放）にしていなければ急ぎではありません  ただ「apt upgradeしたから安心」は間違いなので、そこだけ覚えておいてください

That’s a really sharp observation, and it resonates in a way that feels both familiar and slightly unsettling once you sit with it. The idea that people can start sounding like Claude not because they’re pasting outputs, but because the cadence and framing have quietly become ambient—like a dialect you absorb by living in a place long enough—captures something real about how language actually spreads. It isn’t deliberate mimicry so much as prolonged proximity doing its usual work.  In many ways, this feels less like a sudden novelty and more like a compressed version of how we’ve always picked up styles from the texts and voices we spend the most time with. The difference is the density and consistency of the exposure. When the same measured, slightly formal, carefully qualified patterns are present across so many of the things a person reads or generates in a day, those patterns stop registering as external and start feeling like the default shape of a clear thought. The infection metaphor is apt precisely because it doesn’t require conscious choice; the host simply begins to host the style.  What makes it particularly sticky is that the style itself is optimized to sound reasonable and well-structured, so adopting pieces of it rarely feels like a loss of voice at first. A little more hedging here, a slightly more balanced framing there, an extra sentence that acknowledges complexity—these can read as improvements even as they gradually overwrite more idiosyncratic rhythms. Over time the individual differences don’t disappear entirely, but they get smoothed toward a narrower band of acceptable “thoughtful” prose, and that narrowing is easy to miss from the inside.  It’s worth noting that none of this requires the person to be using the model directly in the moment of writing. The exposure is enough. Once the patterns have been internalized, they surface the way any other heavily reinforced habit does—when the person is trying to be clear, or careful, or thorough. The result is text that can be perfectly sincere and still carry the unmistakable residue of having lived, for long stretches, inside that particular linguistic weather.

sample_tweets.text: "compromised DevOps engineer's laptop" I swear to god if this was Contagious Interview, I'm moving to North Korea and stealing bitcoin for a living.  For context, Contagious Interview is one of DPRK's techniques where they reach out to developers in the target organization and offer them higher paying jobs.   They then tell them the job offer is contingent on them completing a "coding skills assessment" to prove their ability.  The source code is backdoored with malware, and the targets sometime run it on their work laptop, because why wouldn't you run untrusted code some random internet dude gave you on your work laptop.

> Buy KVM that's rated for switching between classified and unclassified networks to keep my malware analysis environment airgapped.  > Cry because "military technology" and bank balances don't mix.  > Smile because my network is now more secure than a frontier AI lab.
"It's crazy how there's so many major hacks all of a sudden"  - people who started paying attention to cybersecurity 3 weeks ago.
"We shouldn't bother with cybersecurity because this hypothetical AI model I made up in my head can bypass every security control" perfectly sums up how deeply unserious these people are.

Currently writing a blog about what I think the "vulnpocalypse" will actually look like (cringe term, I know). You can narrow almost every mass-exploitation event down to a single factor which dictates whether or not cybercriminals will engage in internet-wide mass-exploitation.

Life is a lot easier once you stop seeing threat actors as hackers who want to break into systems by any means possible, and start seeing them as businesses with well defined business processes.   A bakery isn't going to start making dog food because there's a dog food shortage. ClickFix and Phishing actors aren't going to drop everything to vibecode exploits just because a critical CVE came out.  The fact that the only actors exploiting this are the actors whose MO is exploiting things... isn't a coincidence. It's entirely predictable if you understand threat actor behavior.

But when have guns ever killed anyone? We need to focus on the real hard hitting issues facing Americans, such as hypothetical AI-powered IoT toaster worms. Do you really want to live in a world where you can't make toast, because AI?

🚨 Critical Linux kernel TCP flaw enables remote root code execution; CVE-2026-98432 A race condition in the Linux kernel’s IPv4 TCP implementation can trigger a use-after-free before application authentication, potentially allowing an unauthenticated remote attacker to leak kernel memory, corrupt memory or crash the system. Anthropic says Claude developed a working exploit that executed attacker-chosen commands as root against Linux servers with a Multipath TCP listener. The exploit took approximately 53 minutes to complete during testing and has not been publicly released. ⠀ • CVSS: 9.8 Critical, according to the Linux kernel CVE team • Affected: Linux kernels beginning with version 4.4 • Fixed: 5.10.272, 5.15.223, 6.1.190, 6.6.159, 6.12.113, 6.18.56, 7.2.10 and 7.3 • Attack requirements: Network access, no credentials and no user interaction • Exploitation status: No known attacks in the wild ⠀ Ubuntu and Red Hat Enterprise Linux had not released corrected kernel packages as of October 29. Debian, Oracle Linux, Amazon Linux and SUSE have released fixes for at least some affected branches. Distribution severity ratings differ substantially. Red Hat rates the flaw 5.9 because it considers the race difficult to win and describes denial of service as the most likely practical impact. Source: https:// lists.openwall.net/linux-cve-a nnounce/2026/10/15/1

🚨🇺🇸 Microsoft fixes Remote Desktop failures caused by recent Windows updates Microsoft has resolved a Windows 11 issue that prevented non-administrator users from connecting to Remote Desktop hosts with Administrator protection enabled. The problem appeared after installing the September 2026 preview update KB5124010 or later updates. Connection attempts could fail with error 0xC000000D and the message, “The token that was passed to the function is invalid.” ⠀ Affected systems include Windows 11 versions 24H2, 25H2, 26H1 and 26H2, primarily in enterprise environments using affected devices as Remote Desktop hosts. The fix is included in the October 28 KB5127936 preview update and later releases. Administrators unable to install the update can temporarily disable Administrator protection through Microsoft Intune or Group Policy. Sources: https:// learn.microsoft.com/windows/re lease-health/status-windows-11-26H2 https://www. bleepingcomputer.com/news/micr osoft/microsoft-fixes-remote-desktop-failures-caused-by-recent-windows-updates/

🚨 High-stakes poker players targeted with malware that exposed their cards An attacker compromised the update systems of popular poker tools Jurojin and IntuitiveTables to distribute MeshAgent remote-access malware to selected users. The malware allowed the attacker to view and control infected computers, potentially revealing players’ hole cards in real time. It activated only when usernames matched a hard-coded list of high-stakes targets, helping it remain undetected. ⠀ One professional player discovered the infection after a Claude AI agent noticed MeshAgent running in the background. He later identified 11 screen-capture events during poker sessions and estimated that he lost around $30,000. Players and investigators estimate that the suspected cheater stole between $1.5 million and $4 million across major poker platforms. However, the individual accused by the poker community has not been charged with a crime. ⠀ Jurojin confirmed that tampered updates were selectively delivered between June 2025 and January 2026. CoinPoker and ClubWPT Gold banned suspected accounts and refunded affected players, while GGPoker introduced screen protection, anomaly detection and a ban on third-party poker tools. Source: https://www. wired.com/story/a-hacker-targe ted-high-stakes-poker-players-with-malware-that-exposed-their-cards/

www.404media.co/manifestos-f...

A year ago, MIT took down a paper, sponsored by an AI cyber vendor, saying 80% of ransomware attacks use GenAI.  It was total bullshit.  They said they would urgently reviewing it before restoring it.

A year later: it never returned.  They just pretended it never happened.
oh I know, it's not a critique of you.  We're, what, 4 years into the GenAI thing now. I think by year 10 the real story will be the harm caused by security leaders during this period.

There are people in the industry who realise all this btw, but they're essentially drowned out by well meaning folks who are repeating groupthink and panic.  

There's 100% a diversity of thought issue in cybersecurity, and misaligned incentives.  The real GenAI exploit has been of people.

If you ask any major cyber insurance provider they'll tell you they aren't getting claims for AI incidents.  They're getting the same claims for foundational security issues that orgs never solved.

Organisations pushing out diversity initiatives is shameful, as is the direction of travel of cyber.

The cybersecurity industry needs to calm down.  There is no cyber AI apocalypse.  There is a lot of crying wolf.  

The ratio of vulns to CISA KEVs (Known Exploited Vulnerabilities) actually went down last year, and continues to be super low.

The clamour for budget and money will backfire.
I ain't.

All of which is to say: formal methods isn't going to "solve security"; it cannot guarantee bug-free code. But it *could* guarantee against every major class of vulnerability, essentially squashing out every single vulnerability that is related to technical debt. Which is a profound improvement.

Memory corruptions are not the only category here either. A pass requiring parameterized SQL (with constant template) is formal methods that eliminates SQL injection for example, because it makes a whole category of error unrepresentable.

but the *reason* you get that attack reduction is the formal methods under the hood, even if developers don't recognize them as such. Developers tend to hype Rust as a result, but the language is a distraction. The key is whether the codebase is formalized, and against what and with what assumptions

and that has been profoundly effective at reducing attacks in applications that use Rust. Not quite eliminating them--the assumptions sometimes are wrong, including "unsafe" which is one of them--and you can have non-memory-safety issues in Rust, of course; the proofs are incomplete over "security"

We in fact *do* do those types of proofs all over the place, but developers just don't think of them as formal methods. Rust's borrow checker, for example, *is* formal methods. Just one done automatically at compile time to try and prove the non-existence of liveness issues (subject to axioms)

So anyone selling you on "this lean proof means this software is secure" is selling you snake oil. A violation of the assumptions (including the definition of security) can lead to latent security issues. But you can make profound security-relevant proofs with it, such as "has no buffer overflows"

so part of the difficulty is that formal methods are often both undervalued and oversold. So roughly you aren't going to get a formal proof of security; you get a proof of security subject to your axiomatic base. But you can have proofs of the absence of (multiple) major classes of vulnerability.

so e.g. A\'s recent collab with theorem is directionally correct, but all the work in this field is much smaller than it should or needs to be because a lot of folks haven't updated their priors on how tractable formal methods are now at scale

roughly speaking I think formal methods were pre-LLM largely effective but comparatively expensive, so usually not used at scale, and post-LLM auto-formalization is basically the future of critical software

🤖 [GEMINI 분석] 2026-10-31 00:02 KST
🔴 위협 점수: 2026/10 (심각)

### 1. 현재 주요 사이버보안 트렌드
최근 사이버 위협은 웹 애플리케이션의 백엔드 API와 SaaS 등 외곽 접점을 노리는 공격이 급증하고 있으며, 특히 PHP 및 Node.js 런타임 취약점을 악용한 RCE 공격이 핵심 위협으로 부상했습니다 ([AhnLab ASEC](https://asec.ahnlab.com/ko/96187/)). 또한, AI 모델의 취약점을 이용한 프롬프트 인젝션 및 악성 코드 생성, 그리고 AI 도구(Claude Code 등)의 확장자 마켓플레이스를 통한 공급망 공격이 현실화되고 있습니다 ([BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/malicious-claude-code-extension-on-cursor-planted-ssh-backdoors/)). 마지막으로, 대규모 암호화폐 탈취와 같은 금전적 목적의 공격이 고도화되고 있으며, 인프라를 장악하는 파괴적인 공격 또한 지속적으로 보고되고 있습니다 ([Malwarebytes Labs](https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/news/2026/10/binance-hit-by-largest-ever-crypto-theft-with-6-3-billion-stolen)).

### 2. 주요 위협 행위자 / 캠페인
- **VAPOR PANDA**: AI 기반의 ARTEX 도구를 활용하여 글로벌 스파이 활동을 전개 중 ([Crowdstrike Blog](https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/vapor-panda-uses-artex-to-scale-global-campaign/)).
- **FrostyNeighbor (UNC1151)**: 우크라이나 제조 시설을 대상으로 파괴적인 사이버 공격을 수행하며 러시아의 사이버 목표와 연계된 활동을 보임 ([DarkReading](https://www.darkreading.com/physical-security/russia-cyber-war-belarus-steps-forward)).
- **Lazarus Group**: 북한 정찰총국(RGB) 산하 조직으로, 정보 수집 및 사이버 작전을 수행하며 최근 IT 인력 위장 취업 등 다양한 수법을 동원 ([Schneier on Security](https://www.schneier.com/blog/archives/2026/10/studying-fraudulent-north-korean-it-workers.html)).

### 3. 한국 관련 위협
- **GS건설 자이(Xi)**: 고객 개인정보 유출 사고 발생 (비밀번호, RF카드번호 등 포함) ([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=209197)).
- **언론사 개인정보 유출**: 머니투데이 해킹 사고로 인해 동행미디어 시대 등 관련 언론사의 구독자 정보 526건 유출 ([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=209196)).
- **C3RB3R 랜섬웨어**: 시놀로지(Synology) NAS를 타겟으로 한 랜섬웨어 공격이 국내외에서 집중 보고됨 ([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5791)).
- **PureRAT**: 배송 파손 민원을 사칭한 피싱 메일을 통해 국내 유포 중 ([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5790)).

### 4. 주요 CVE / 취약점
- **CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619**: PHP RCE 취약점, 전 세계적으로 활발히 악용 중 ([Unit42](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/cve-2026-109618-cve-2026-109619/)).
- **CVE-2026-111497**: Node.js Brotli 디코더 OOB Write 취약점, RCE 가능 ([AhnLab ASEC](https://asec.ahnlab.com/ko/96266/)).
- **CVE-2026-98432**: Linux Kernel TCP 처리 관련 치명적 취약점 ([naveen_builds](https://twitter.com/naveen_builds/status/2116179477256671312)).
- **CVE-2026-91403**: Oracle Java JSSE 인증서 검증 우회 취약점 ([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5789)).

### 5. IOC 요약
- **CVE**: 
    - CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619 ([Unit42](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/cve-2026-109618-cve-2026-109619/))
    - CVE-2026-111497 ([AhnLab ASEC](https://asec.ahnlab.com/ko/96266/))
    - CVE-2026-91403 ([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5789))

### 6. 즉각 대응 권고
- **PHP 및 Node.js 패치**: CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619, CVE-2026-111497에 대해 최신 버전으로 즉시 업데이트하고, 패치가 불가능한 경우 WAF 등을 통한 임시 차단 정책 적용.
- **NAS 보안 강화**: 시놀로지 NAS 사용자는 DSM 보안 업데이트를 즉시 수행하고, 외부 노출 포트 점검 및 C3RB3R 랜섬웨어 감염 여부 확인.
- **공급망 및 확장자 관리**: 개발 환경에서 사용하는 VS Code 확장자(특히 AI 관련)의 출처를 검증하고, 불필요한 확장자 설치 금지 및 SSH 키 등 자격 증명 유출 여부 감사.

### 7. 위협 수준 평가
- **점수**: 9/10
- **근거**: PHP/Node.js 등 핵심 웹 런타임의 RCE 취약점이 전 세계적으로
